entries.sense_en: pressuring or bullying someone into doing what you want, here into giving a lower price

synonyms.nuance: Neutral word for arguing over a price; bulldoze adds force and pushiness.
synonyms.example: She haggled over the price of the fish.

synonyms.nuance: Stronger, about intimidating someone with stern words or looks.
synonyms.example: He browbeat the clerk into a refund.

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday verb; less vivid and less aggressive than bulldoze.
synonyms.example: Don't pressure me into buying it.

entries.tip_ko: 원래 '불도저로 밀다'라는 뜻인데, 여기서는 사람을 윽박질러 원하는 걸 얻어내는 비유적 의미입니다.

entries.sense_en: an unspoken suggestion or accusation that someone has a bad quality

synonyms.nuance: Open and direct; imputation is quieter, often only implied.
A sly, indirect hint; closest in feeling, but slightly more sneaky.
synonyms.example: I resent the insinuation that I lied.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral: something suggested without being said; not necessarily negative.
synonyms.example: The implication was that we were late.

entries.sense_en: extreme unwillingness to spend money; stinginess

synonyms.nuance: Everyday and plainly critical; parsimony is formal and literary.
Positive: careful, sensible saving. Parsimony suggests going too far.
synonyms.example: Her frugality paid for the house.

synonyms.nuance: Approving word for wise use of money, often a virtue.

entries.tip_ko: frugal/thrifty는 칭찬, stingy/parsimonious는 흉보는 말이라는 차이를 기억하세요.

entries.sense_en: bargaining in a very tight, stingy way over every cent

synonyms.nuance: Modern informal term for saving every small amount; slightly mocking.
Focuses on tough negotiation, not necessarily on being mean with money.
synonyms.example: After hard bargaining, they agreed on a price.

entries.tip_ko: 여기서 close는 '가까운'이 아니라 '돈에 인색한'이라는 옛 뜻이며 발음은 /kloʊs/ (s 소리)입니다.

entries.sense_en: to drop your body heavily and loosely onto something

synonyms.nuance: Suggests sinking because of tiredness or sadness, often staying bent over.
Stronger; falling because you have no strength left.
Casual and lighter, often with a soft sound; less emotional.
synonyms.example: The kids plopped down on the rug.

entries.sense_en: to cause something to begin, here to give rise to a thought

synonyms.nuance: Neutral, natural choice for causing a thought or reaction.
synonyms.example: The news prompted a lot of questions.

synonyms.nuance: Usually causes a strong or negative reaction.
Vivid, informal; something starts suddenly, like a fire.

entries.tip_ko: 현대 영어에서 instigate는 주로 싸움·폭동 등 나쁜 일을 '선동하다'에 쓰입니다. 여기서는 작가가 일부러 거창한 단어를 쓴 유머입니다.

entries.sense_en: to be the largest or most common part

synonyms.nuance: Suggests winning out over something else, or being widespread.
Stronger; implies control or power, not just larger number.
Strictly about quantity: there are more of one kind.
synonyms.example: Women outnumber men in the class.

entries.sense_en: becoming calmer or less strong, here moving from sobs to sniffles

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrasal verb, usually about a person's feelings.
synonyms.example: Give her time to calm down.

synonyms.nuance: Formal, often used for storms, pain or noise.
Gentle word for pain, pressure or tension becoming less.
synonyms.example: The pain eased after an hour.

entries.sense_en: to be too extreme (here: too shabby) to describe in words

synonyms.nuance: Plain version; beggar description is literary and often ironic.
Very close modern equivalent, slightly less old-fashioned.
Everyday and usually emotional, often positive.

entries.tip_ko: beggar가 '거지'가 아니라 동사로 쓰였습니다. 작가는 그 '거지'라는 말이 거지 단속반(mendicancy squad)을 경계하고 있을 만큼, 이 집이 거의 거지 수준이라는 말장난을 합니다.

entries.sense_en: begging; living by asking people for money

synonyms.nuance: The ordinary word; mendicancy is formal and Latin-based.
synonyms.example: Begging is banned in the station.

synonyms.nuance: Having no home or job and wandering; a legal term, not only begging.
Extreme poverty itself, not the act of asking for money.

entries.tip_ko: 'mendicancy squad'는 거리의 거지를 단속하던 경찰반을 말합니다.

entries.sense_en: the woman in charge of a household (said grandly, and ironically, of Della sobbing on a shabby couch)

synonyms.nuance: Polite, old-fashioned phrase with the same meaning; less formal-sounding.
synonyms.example: Is the lady of the house at home?

synonyms.nuance: Plain word for a married woman who runs the home; no grandness.
The woman who receives guests, not the one who runs the house.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 mistress는 주로 '(유부남의) 정부(情婦)'라는 뜻으로 쓰이니 주의하세요. 여기서는 '안주인'이라는 옛 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: a small entrance area just inside the front door of a building
entries.sense_ko: (건물 현관 안쪽의) 현관 홀, 입구 공간

synonyms.nuance: A larger public entrance space, as in hotels or offices.
synonyms.example: Meet me in the hotel lobby.

synonyms.nuance: Everyday American word for the area by the door of a home.
synonyms.example: Leave your shoes in the entryway.

synonyms.nuance: Slightly elegant word, for homes, theaters or hotels.

entries.sense_en: to get something to work or happen by gentle, patient effort

synonyms.nuance: Used for people, with reasons; coax is gentler and works on things too.
Coaxing with flattery, often slightly manipulative.
synonyms.example: She wheedled money out of her dad.

synonyms.nuance: Formal; persistent sweet talk to make someone agree.

entries.tip_ko: 발음은 /koʊks/로 '코욱스'에 가깝습니다. '코악스'가 아닙니다.

entries.sense_en: belonging to it; connected with it (very old legal-sounding language)

synonyms.nuance: The plain modern way to say the same thing.
synonyms.example: a garden belonging to the house

synonyms.nuance: Formal but still used; means 'related to' rather than 'owned by'.
Physical or official connection; very natural for a card on a door.
synonyms.example: a note attached to the door

entries.tip_ko: O. Henry가 일부러 법률 문서 같은 딱딱한 말을 써서 초라한 우편함을 과장되게 묘사하는 유머입니다.

entries.sense_en: displayed proudly for everyone to see, like a flag in the wind

synonyms.nuance: Showing off, often in a way others find annoying.
Neutral; no pride or showiness implied.
synonyms.example: Their name was displayed on the door.

synonyms.nuance: Informal and a bit critical; wanting admiration.

entries.sense_en: modest; not trying to look important

synonyms.nuance: General word; can also mean small or not expensive.
Stresses low status or a low opinion of oneself; can be moral praise.
Informal; quiet and not showy, used for events or style too.

entries.tip_ko: 여기서는 긴 'Dillingham'을 소박한 'D.' 한 글자로 줄이려 한다는 농담입니다. 사람이 아니라 이름 글자를 의인화했습니다.

entries.sense_en: of excellent, genuine quality (from sterling silver, which is pure)

synonyms.nuance: Plain praise; sterling adds the idea of genuine and reliable.
Informal-ish, top quality in its class.
Stresses being real, not fake, rather than high quality.

entries.tip_ko: 영국 화폐 '파운드 스털링'과 같은 단어로, 원래 '순은의'라는 뜻에서 '진짜로 훌륭한'이 되었습니다.

entries.sense_en: a tall, narrow mirror hung on the wall between two windows
entries.sense_ko: (창문 사이 벽에 거는) 좁고 긴 거울

synonyms.nuance: Modern term for a mirror showing your whole body; not tied to windows.
synonyms.example: a full-length mirror on the closet door

synonyms.nuance: Old-fashioned word for any mirror.

entries.tip_ko: 여기서 pier는 '부두'가 아니라 창과 창 사이의 벽 기둥을 뜻합니다.

entries.sense_en: able to move quickly and easily

synonyms.nuance: Similar, but often about quick, light fingers or feet.
About bending easily, not speed.
Everyday and general; no sense of grace or skill.

entries.tip_ko: 미국식 발음은 /ˈædʒəl/로 '애절'에 가깝고, '애자일'(/ˈædʒaɪl/)은 영국식 발음입니다. 몸을 비춰 보려면 곡예사처럼 날렵해야 한다는 과장 유머입니다.

entries.sense_en: running lengthwise, from top to bottom

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word for up-and-down direction.
Informal; along the long side of something.

entries.tip_ko: 과학 용어를 일부러 써서, 좁은 거울에 몸을 조금씩 비춰 봐야 하는 처지를 우스꽝스럽게 표현했습니다.

entries.sense_en: an idea or picture in your mind of what something is like

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; conception is formal and more complete.
synonyms.example: I have no idea what he looks like.

synonyms.nuance: A feeling or picture, often based on little information.
A belief or idea, often vague or mistaken.
synonyms.example: a romantic notion of city life

entries.sense_en: to make something seem less valuable in comparison

synonyms.nuance: Making someone or something seem unimportant, usually with words.
Idiom: being so much better that the other looks poor.
synonyms.example: Her cooking puts mine to shame.

synonyms.nuance: Economic or formal; reducing the actual or felt value.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 depreciate는 주로 '(자동차·화폐 등의) 가치가 떨어지다'라는 경제 용어로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a small waterfall; here, hair falling down in long waves

synonyms.nuance: Plain word, usually literal and larger.
A violent, fast rush of water; much stronger.
Neutral, smooth continuous movement.

entries.sense_en: to lose confidence for a moment and hesitate

synonyms.nuance: Neutral pause before acting; falter adds weakness or loss of nerve.
Being unsure between choices, often for longer.
Physical tripping, or making mistakes when speaking.

entries.sense_en: to become calm and in control again

synonyms.nuance: Informal, often said to someone upset; stronger emotion involved.
synonyms.example: Pull yourself together and go in.

synonyms.nuance: Formal, stresses a calm face and manner.
Physical: resting after running, like Della panting on the stairs.
synonyms.example: Let me catch my breath first.

entries.sense_en: skilled because of long experience

synonyms.nuance: General; focuses on time spent rather than smooth skill.
Highest level of skill or knowledge.
Experienced over many years, often through hard situations.

entries.tip_ko: 'a practised hand'는 '익숙한 솜씨'라는 관용 표현입니다. 미국식 철자는 practiced입니다.

entries.sense_en: passed quickly and lightly, like dancing steps

synonyms.nuance: The common modern idiom for time passing quickly.
Time passing without being noticed.

entries.tip_ko: trip은 '넘어지다'가 아니라 '가볍게 춤추듯 걷다'라는 옛 문학적 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: a messy metaphor that mixes images that don't fit together

synonyms.nuance: The standard term today; 'hashed' is the author's playful version.
synonyms.example: 'We'll burn that bridge when we come to it' is a mixed metaphor.

synonyms.nuance: An overused phrase; not necessarily mixed or illogical.

entries.tip_ko: 시간이 '발걸음(tripped)'과 '날개(wings)'를 동시에 가져서 비유가 엉켰다고 작가가 스스로 농담하는 부분입니다. hash는 '잘게 다져 섞은 요리'입니다.

entries.sense_en: searching a place very thoroughly, turning everything over

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; no sense of mess or urgency.
synonyms.example: I searched the drawer for my keys.

synonyms.nuance: Searching very carefully and widely; no damage implied.
Searching through a mess of things with your hands, casually.

entries.tip_ko: ransack은 도둑이 '집을 뒤집어 놓다'에도 자주 쓰여 어지럽힌다는 느낌이 있습니다. 여기서는 과장된 유머입니다.

entries.sense_en: a short chain that attaches a pocket watch to clothing

synonyms.nuance: Plain descriptive term for the same object.
A band of leather or cloth, like Jim's cheap one.

entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 fob은 주로 '열쇠고리(key fob)'나 출입용 전자 태그를 가리킵니다.

entries.sense_en: simple and plain in style, with no extra decoration

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; chaste adds a sense of purity and good taste.
Modern praise for quiet, elegant design.
Very plain, sometimes to the point of feeling cold or harsh.

entries.tip_ko: chaste의 기본 뜻은 '순결한'이지만, 디자인에 쓰면 '장식 없이 단정한'이라는 뜻이 됩니다.

entries.sense_en: showy and attractive on the surface but cheap and without real value

synonyms.nuance: Too bright and colorful; the everyday criticism of showy things.
Informal; designed to impress, often expensive-looking.
Cheap, low-quality and tasteless, often also morally low.

entries.tip_ko: 라틴어 meretrix(돈을 받고 몸을 파는 여자)에서 온 말로, '돈만 노린 싸구려 겉치레'라는 강한 비난입니다. 비슷해 보이는 merit(장점)의 긍정적인 뜻과 혼동하지 마세요.

entries.sense_en: secretly, so that others don't notice

synonyms.nuance: Neutral standard adverb.
British-leaning idiom; keeping it hidden, often not wrong.
synonyms.example: He told me on the quiet.

synonyms.nuance: Formal; nervous, guilty secrecy.
synonyms.example: He glanced furtively at the door.

entries.sense_en: a wild, excited feeling of happiness (not from alcohol here)

synonyms.nuance: Intense happiness, often short-lived.
Great joy after success; less wild.
Everyday, general word.
synonyms.example: The kids couldn't hide their excitement.

entries.tip_ko: 보통은 '술에 취함'이라는 뜻이라 문맥을 잘 봐야 합니다.

entries.sense_en: careful, sensible thinking about the results of your actions

synonyms.nuance: Focuses on avoiding danger rather than good judgment.
Everyday phrase for practical wisdom.
synonyms.example: She had the good sense to leave early.

synonyms.nuance: Judgment about what to say or do, especially keeping things private.

entries.sense_en: the serious damage caused by something

synonyms.nuance: Plain, neutral word; ravages is dramatic.
Total, widespread destruction.
The cost or harm over time, as in 'take a toll'.
synonyms.example: Stress took its toll on her.

entries.tip_ko: 'the ravages of time/war'처럼 쓰는 거창한 말을 머리 손질에 쓴 과장 유머입니다.

entries.sense_en: staying away from school without permission

synonyms.nuance: Informal American idiom for skipping school.
synonyms.example: We played hooky and went to the beach.

synonyms.nuance: Neutral; not there, for any reason.
synonyms.example: He was absent due to illness.

synonyms.nuance: Everyday phrase, often for one lesson only.

entries.tip_ko: 짧은 곱슬머리가 된 델라가 '말썽꾸러기 남학생'처럼 보인다는 뜻입니다.

entries.sense_en: a hunting dog that stands perfectly still when it smells birds
entries.sense_ko: 세터(사냥감 냄새를 맡으면 꼼짝 않고 서는 사냥개)

synonyms.nuance: A similar hunting dog that points its nose toward the game.
synonyms.example: The pointer froze in the grass.

synonyms.nuance: Hunting dog that chases by scent; moves, not freezes.

entries.sense_en: very clear and obvious (ironic: the fact is plain, yet Jim still cannot take it in)

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word; patent is formal and literary.
Clear from signs or evidence; formal.
synonyms.example: It was evident she was tired.

synonyms.nuance: Obvious in a bad, shameless way.

entries.tip_ko: '특허'의 patent와 같은 단어이며, 미국에서는 보통 /ˈpætənt/ '패턴트'로 발음합니다(영국에서는 '페이턴트'도 흔함). 뻔한 사실을 '아무리 머리를 짜내도' 못 알아듣는다는 과장된 유머입니다.

entries.sense_en: slowly and with great effort, as if thinking were hard work

synonyms.nuance: Careful effort to get every detail right; positive, not slow-witted.
Plain phrase; no sense of slow, heavy effort.
Speaking with pauses and breaks, unsure of the words.

entries.tip_ko: labor(노동)에서 온 말로, 말 한마디 하는 데도 '중노동'을 하는 것 같다는 과장입니다. 뒤의 'the hardest mental labor'와 짝을 이룹니다.

entries.sense_en: held someone closely in your arms

synonyms.nuance: Formal word for hugging; enfold stresses wrapping around completely.
Everyday, casual.
Long, warm, affectionate hug, often lying down.

entries.sense_en: careful not to embarrass others or draw attention

synonyms.nuance: Careful not to upset people, especially in speech.
Not obvious; about style or method rather than politeness.
General good manners; no idea of keeping private.

entries.tip_ko: discrete(별개의)와 발음이 같아 헷갈리기 쉽습니다. 철자를 구분하세요.

entries.sense_en: very close, careful examination (here jokingly: pretending to study something unimportant so as not to stare)

synonyms.nuance: Official checking for problems.
General careful look; neutral.
Looking to learn or understand; less intense.

entries.tip_ko: 'discreet scrutiny of some inconsequential object'는 '괜히 딴 데를 열심히 쳐다보자'는 익살스러운 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: the wise men from the East who brought gifts to baby Jesus

synonyms.nuance: The everyday English name in Christmas stories.
synonyms.example: We three kings... the wise men

synonyms.nuance: Any very wise people, not tied to the Bible.

entries.tip_ko: magus의 복수형으로 '메이자이'처럼 발음합니다. magic과 어원이 같습니다. 이야기 끝에서 작가는 '어리석은' 두 사람이야말로 진짜 현자(magi)라고 뒤집어 말합니다.

entries.sense_en: not important at all

synonyms.nuance: Common word for small and unimportant matters.
Too small in size or effect to matter; neutral.
Less important than others, but still something.

entries.sense_en: a clever person who is good at making quick, funny remarks

synonyms.nuance: Informal; someone who jokes a lot, not necessarily clever.
Someone who is funny, often as a job.
Skilled with words, not necessarily funny.

entries.tip_ko: 보통은 '재치'라는 셀 수 없는 명사지만, 'a wit'처럼 쓰면 '재치 있는 사람'이 됩니다.

entries.sense_en: to make clear or explain (a pun: the 'dark' statement will be 'lit up')

synonyms.nuance: Plain everyday word; no image of light.
Making something less confusing; formal but common.
Idiom with the same light image; often about causes or facts.
synonyms.example: The letter sheds light on his motives.

entries.tip_ko: dark assertion(알쏭달쏭한 말)과 illuminated(빛을 비추다 → 밝혀지다)를 짝지은 말장난입니다.

entries.sense_en: to make someone confused, worried or upset for a while

synonyms.nuance: Informal: to confuse or shock someone suddenly.
Deliberately tricking; in modern use 'you had me going' often means 'you fooled me'.
synonyms.example: You fooled me for a minute!

entries.modern: why I was thrown at first
entries.tip_ko: 오늘날 'You had me going!'은 주로 '깜빡 속았잖아!'라는 뜻의 구어로 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: quick and skillful in movement, especially fingers

synonyms.nuance: Quick and skillful, stressing accuracy.
Usually about the whole body moving easily.
General speed only.

entries.tip_ko: 'White fingers and nimble'처럼 형용사를 명사 뒤에 두는 것은 시적인 어순입니다. 보통은 'nimble white fingers'.

entries.sense_en: an old word used to express sadness or regret

synonyms.nuance: The normal modern word; alas is literary or jokingly old-fashioned.
Everyday adverb with the same feeling.

entries.sense_en: making something necessary

synonyms.nuance: Common formal word; needed by rule or situation.
Informal phrasal verb; also used for celebrating.
Stronger; needs a lot of effort or attention.

entries.tip_ko: 'the lord of the flat(집주인 나리)'가 짐을 달래야 했다는 과장된 표현입니다.

entries.sense_en: wanted something deeply, with a sad, longing feeling

synonyms.nuance: Very close; yearn is more poetic and aching.
synonyms.example: He longed to see her again.

synonyms.nuance: Longing so much that you become sad or weak.
Wanting so much it feels painful.

entries.tip_ko: 'yearn over'는 옛 표현이고 지금은 'yearn for'를 씁니다.

entries.sense_en: a woman's long hair (poetic)

synonyms.nuance: The ordinary word.
Also poetic; pieces or curls of hair.
A thick, long mass of hair, like a horse's; playful.

entries.sense_en: greatly wanted; longed for (the combs Della had admired for so long)
entries.sense_ko: 몹시 탐내던, 오래 갖고 싶어 하던

synonyms.nuance: Wanted by many people; coveted stresses one person's strong private longing.
Warm and wistful, with no hint of greed; coveted can suggest envy.
Already owned and valued highly, not just wanted.

entries.tip_ko: 발음은 /ˈkʌvɪt/ '커빗'입니다. '코벳'이 아닙니다.

entries.sense_en: to decorate or make more beautiful

synonyms.nuance: Everyday word, for rooms, cakes, trees.
Adding details to make something fancier, also stories.
Literary: to make beautiful simply by being there.

entries.tip_ko: 'the tresses that should have adorned the coveted adornments'는 거꾸로 된 말장난입니다. 머리를 꾸며야 할 빗을 머리가 꾸민다고 뒤집어 표현했습니다.

entries.sense_en: finally, after some time

synonyms.nuance: The common modern word.
Adds relief that the wait is over.
Everyday and neutral.

entries.tip_ko: at length는 '길게, 자세히(talk at length)'라는 뜻도 있으니 문맥으로 구별하세요.

entries.sense_en: burned slightly on the surface

synonyms.nuance: Burning more, leaving a brown mark.
General word, any degree.
Burned black.

entries.tip_ko: sing(노래하다)과 헷갈리지 마세요. singe는 /sɪndʒ/ '신지', singed는 '신지드'입니다.

entries.sense_en: full of strong, warm feeling

synonyms.nuance: Very close; more common in everyday speech.
Keen to do something; lighter feeling.
Intense and sincere, often about belief or hope.

entries.sense_en: something excellent (old informal slang)

synonyms.nuance: Informal praise for a fine example of something.
Something small and precious.
